A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BECAME with the same authors, algorithm, and experimental framework. The complete main texts and Appendices A–C are readable, and corresponding equations, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original BECAME experiments and reproduced baseline results, including accuracy and forgetting measurements in Tables 1–3 and additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds anytime-accuracy results, comparisons without gradient projection, and detailed memory measurements in Tables 9–12.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the two training stages, Fisher-based precision updates, and the adaptive merging coefficient in Eq. 20 are unchanged. Removing gradient projection is an added ablation, not a replacement of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100, MiniImageNet, TinyImageNet, 5-Datasets, and CIFAR-100 Superclass. The latter two already appear in v1 Appendix C.1. New evaluations retain this coverage and change metrics or training controls.

E2.justification: V2 Table 11 introduces a Finetune comparator in the new comparison without gradient projection, alongside the existing 1/t, CoMA, and CoFiMA strategies. Comparator membership in the original benchmark and merging comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds AAA evaluation and a control omitting the first training stage. Appendix B.4 replaces the stated NSCL-based schedule of 80 epochs with decay at epochs 30 and 60 by loss-triggered halving after three stagnant epochs, stopping at the third trigger, with an 80-epoch cap. This establishes a reported setting change, not that experiments were rerun. Existing splits, architectures, and preprocessing remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a substantive component ablation testing adaptive merging without gradient projection on CIFAR-100 and MiniImageNet. Appendix C.4 additionally decomposes memory overhead by storage category and training stage. These address component attribution and resource costs beyond the retained coefficient-sensitivity, task-balance, and transfer analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions state five random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting, while Table 8 retains its three dataset orders. Existing uncertainty summaries remain unchanged; no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for AAA, merging without gradient projection, and memory components in Tables 9–12; Table 11 reports 65.03% and 64.75% ACC for adaptive merging. Original benchmark scores remain unchanged, and v1 Table 9 becomes v2 Table 13. New repeated ACC entries introduce unexplained discrepancies: 58.77 versus 58.57 for Adam-NSCL on TinyImageNet, and 70.69 versus 70.06 for SGP+Ours on MiniImageNet. These do not establish performance improvements.

T1.justification: V1 informally motivates replacing the previous optimum with the gradient-projected parameters. V2 Section 3.4 adds a substantial attempted proof using Taylor expansion and eigendecomposition, Eqs. 22–26, to establish invariance of the quadratic penalty. The argument has gaps: approximate loss preservation becomes exact equality, and positive semidefiniteness is incorrectly said to force every component of Qd to zero.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction now explicitly qualify the optimal closed-form coefficient as based on the Laplace approximation. The main claims about adaptive stability–plasticity balancing, compatibility with gradient-projection methods, and superior benchmark performance are retained.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new ablation as supporting adaptive merging without gradient projection and discusses agreement between AAA and ACC trends. It also attributes additional first-stage memory to expanded feature spaces and identifies the precision matrix as second-stage storage overhead. Existing explanations of limited gains on 5-Datasets and Superclass remain.

D1.justification: V1 promises code release upon acceptance; v2 reports public availability and supplies a repository address. V2 also revises scheduler and stopping instructions in Appendix B.4, specifies the inherited configuration for the new ablation, and documents memory categories. Hardware, architecture details, and GPM hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a model-merging overview covering task vectors, regression/Fisher weighting, interference mitigation, and heterogeneous models. RegMean, DARE, DAMC, and FuseLLM are newly discussed, but several citations render as question marks. The bibliography and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized qualifications and explanations, correspondence and publication information, an acknowledgement, and an expanded appendix roadmap with separate AAA and gradient-projection-ablation subsections.

P2.justification: V2 adds tables displaying ACC alongside AAA, comparisons without gradient projection, and a structured memory breakdown. Existing figures retain their graphical content but are redistributed across pages; the previous efficiency Table 9 becomes Table 13. The overall visual design remains consistent.

improvement.justification: The new component ablation, memory accounting, explicit approximation qualification, and reported code access provide a modest net gain in empirical scrutiny and reproducibility. The benefit is limited by gaps in the added proof, unclear indexing and normalization in the AAA formula, inconsistent repeated accuracy values, and unresolved citations. These weaknesses prevent a substantial improvement, while the useful controls and disclosures strengthen the otherwise retained paper.
